Subject: Production: P95 latency jump + 5xx after last-night model update

Kimberly —

We rolled the new model variant with qprofile v2 last night (per our scheduled window). Since ~08:45 this morning we're seeing a sharp P95 increase and an uptick in 5xxs:
- Baseline P95 before deploy: ~180ms; current: 1.2s (clear spike across endpoints).
- 5xx rate: from ~0.9% to ~3.6% over last 30m.
- Throughput: sustained throughput is down ~18% despite same request rate.

We've attached a quick P95 graph and a short error sample. Errors look like transient decode stalls and occasional kv-cache timeouts in the logs. This aligns with the time the qprofile variant became active for our v2 route.

We need immediate remediation: can Redwood roll ClearBay back to the prior qprofile/variant while we investigate? This is customer-facing so the CRO is on the thread. We're ready to join a bridge.

--
Alex Moreno
SRE Lead, ClearBay Financial

On Sun, Oct 18, 2026 at 09:50, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai> wrote:
> "P95 from ~180ms to 1.2s; 5xx from 0.9% to 3.6%; errors look like decode stalls and kv-cache timeouts."

Quick triage from runtime: we reproduced a latency tail locally when running the same model with qprofile v2 under a read-heavy KV-cache workload. Root cause hypothesis: qprofile v2 enables a new int8 decode kernel and a slightly different KV cache eviction heuristic which together increase cache miss amplification for longer context sequences — that increases decoding retries and occasional stalls (observable as transient 5xx).

Immediate recommended plan:
- Step 0 (now): start a 10% canary rollback to qprofile v1-stable on ClearBay prod route (low-risk path, safe rollback).
- Step 1 (after 5–10 minutes): check P95 and 5xx; if P95 drops toward baseline and 5xx normalizes, promote rollback to 100%.
- Step 2: snapshot full telemetry and attach qprofile v2 diff (sending patch) for postmortem; run a deterministic test harness to reproduce once traffic is back to baseline.

Rollback command (ops): pin_variant --customer clearbay --route generate --variant qprofile=v1-stable --commit "rollback-20261018-clearbay"

Risk: if ClearBay has route-level tokenization tweaks dependent on v2 behavior, minor output shifts possible. We'll coordinate an immediate validation test set with ClearBay before full promote.

I'll be on the bridge and can own the runtime rollback. Attaching diff: qprofile-v2-diff.patch

—Rishi
Senior Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime

Actions authorized now:

We need a crisp postmortem with root cause, what went wrong in the qprofile test coverage, and a remediation plan (better canary thresholds, perf harness, and auto-rollback on P95 > 250ms).
